name: Significant location change
plain: A low power way to learn that the device moved a long distance, even when the app is closed.
meaning: Wakes the app after the person moves about 500 meters or changes cell towers, so it can rebuild a movement history cheaply. iOS relaunches apps for it; Android uses geofences and activity transitions.

android.store_policy: Play: background location declaration and review
android.api_surface: No exact analog; use geofences or Fused low power updates
android.note: Approximate analog via Geofencing API or passive location requests

ios.prompt_ui: Always prompt after When In Use
ios.note: Updates when the position changes by about 500 m and at least about 5 min apart (typical)

limits.headline: Can learn that you moved a long way, about 500 meters, even with the app closed
limits.user_action: You allow Always location, or turn on a feature that follows trips and places loosely
can: Learn you have moved to a new area, using very little battery
Wake up in the background when you travel far enough
Use that move as a cue to refresh nearby results
cannot: Follow your exact path or speed
Update more often than about every 5 minutes
Run at all if you did not allow Always location
Match this exactly on Android, which has only a rough substitute through geofencing
limits.differs: iPhone has a built in significant change service. Android only has an approximate version through geofences or passive location.

story.what_it_is: A very low power way for an app to learn that you moved a long distance, even while closed.

marketing.name: Significant location change
marketing.pitch: Apple describes this service as a battery friendly way to be notified when a device moves a meaningful distance.

story.for_you: You never see it. An app quietly notes that you have moved to a new area, so your weather or traffic card is right when you open it. It needs your Always location choice.
story.for_makers: Makers can rebuild a rough history of movement without keeping GPS on. It supports commute and weather features, and it is also a way to build a long term travel profile.

use_cases.example: A trip app notices you landed in a new city and shows your hotel and a local guide.
A traffic app learns your usual commute and warns you about delays before you leave.
A weather app shifts its alerts to the new town you drove into.
An ad network updates which city a device is in so local ads match.
A banking app sees you suddenly in another country and tightens checks on card use.
A game reopens with local events for the city you are visiting.

risks: Builds a long term movement history
Hard to see when it is on
story.android_note: There is no exact copy. Apps use geofences or passive location instead.
story.ios_note: Updates arrive when you move about 500 meters, and at least about five minutes apart.
